newsitem.title: USA: First-time jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: First-time jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: The number of people filing new claims for unemployment benefits in late April rose by 28,000, the government said on Thursday, well above economists expectations.

In a week that saw layoffs from severe flooding and the automobile industry, the Labour Department said 347,000 people filed first-time claims for unemployment insurance benefits in the week ended April 26, up from 319,000 claims in the previous week.

Large sections of Grand Forks and its sister city East Grand Forks were submerged more than a week ago by the swollen Red River, while the auto industry saw strikes at Chrysler Corp. and General Motors Corp. this month.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 325,000 in the April 26 week.

The rise brought the average weekly rate of new claims over the past four weeks -- a more accurate measurement of employment trends than the more volatile weekly numbers -- to 330,500, up from 321,750 in the prior four-week period.

Total benefit rolls rose 2,000 to 2.273 million in the week ended April 19, the latest period for which those figures were available. That was up from 2.271 million the prior week, the department said.
Labour said two states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended April 19, the latest period for which data are available.
Missouri reported 2,263 additional claims because of layoffs in the transportation industry. Rhode Island, with 1,053, had no comment on the increase.
Fourteen states and one territory reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the April 19 week.
The largest included North Carolina, with 5,239 fewer claims; Texas, with 4,103; Pennsylvania, with 4,033; New York, with 3,250; Tennessee, with 3,102; Alabama, 2,981; and Wisconsin, with 2,318.

North Carolina cited fewer layoffs in the textile, furniture and transportation equipment industries. Pennyslvania had fewer layoffs in the trade, food and stone/clay/glass industries. Tennessee cited fewer layoffs in the food, textile, apparel, rubber/plastics, industrial machinery, trade and service industries.

Alabama reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and manufacturing. Wisconsin had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries and manufacturing. New York and Texas had no comment.
The Labour Department said the last time initial claims had reached this level was for the Jan. 4 week when first-time applications totalled 365,000.
The seasonally adjusted four-week moving average was at its highest since the Jan. 25 week, when claims were reported at 339,750, Labour said.
